units.source_text: 然而，还有比寒酸的生活更让他憎恨的事，那就是贫穷所致的虚伪。

en.t: Yet there was something he hated even more than a shabby life: the hypocrisy born of poverty.

units.source_text: 母亲用“风月堂”的盒子装蛋糕送亲戚，

en.t: His mother would put cakes in a box from Fugetsudo and send them to relatives,

units.source_text: 但是那里面装的根本就不是“风月堂”的和菓子，而是附近点心铺的蜂蜜蛋糕啊！

en.t: but what was inside was not Fugetsudo wagashi at all; it was honey cake from a nearby sweet shop!

units.source_text: 父亲也是如此，他总是教育大家“勤俭尚武”。

en.t: His father was the same, always teaching everyone to be frugal and martial in spirit.

units.source_text: 但是，倘若父亲要提到训诫的话，唯有一本陈旧的《玉篇》，除此之外就连《汉和辞典》也算是“奢侈文弱”！

en.t: But when his father spoke of moral instruction, there was only one old copy of Yupian; anything else, even a Chinese-Japanese dictionary, counted as luxurious and weak!

units.source_text: 不仅仅是这样，信辅自己也很懂得说谎，而且说谎的本事并不逊于他的父母。

en.t: Nor was that all: Shinsuke himself knew very well how to lie, and his skill at lying was no worse than his parents'.

units.source_text: 他每个月的零用钱是五十钱，倘若能够多弄到零花钱，即使只多一分钱，他也会拿去买喜欢的图书和杂志。

en.t: His monthly allowance was fifty sen, and if he could get any extra spending money, even a single sen more, he would use it to buy the books and magazines he liked.

units.source_text: 他会为此撒谎，说钱弄丢啦！

en.t: For that purpose he would lie, saying that he had lost the money!
He needed to buy a notebook!
He needed to pay class fees!

units.source_text: ——总而言之，想方设法用一切借口，骗父母的钱。

en.t: In short, he used every excuse he could devise to cheat money out of his parents.

units.source_text: 哪怕是这样，钱还是有不够用的时候，他只能使出浑身解数博得父母的欢心，以便早点拿到下个月的零花钱。

en.t: Even so, there were times when the money was still not enough, and he had no choice but to do everything he could to please his parents so that he could get next month's allowance early.

units.source_text: 他最喜欢博取宠爱他的老母亲的欢心。

en.t: What he liked most was winning the favor of his old mother, who doted on him.

units.source_text: 当然，无论是他自己说谎，还是父母说谎，对他来说不都是愉快的是行情。

en.t: Of course, whether he lied himself or his parents lied, it was not all pleasant for him.

units.source_text: 不过，他还是一如既往地说谎，大胆而狡诈的撒谎。

en.t: Nevertheless, he went on lying as ever, lying boldly and cunningly.

units.source_text: 因此撒谎对他来说，是比什么都特别重要的事，他还能因此感到病态的愉悦——一种好似杀死什么一样的愉悦。

en.t: Thus lying was, for him, more specially important than anything else, and from it he could feel a morbid pleasure, a pleasure like having killed something.

units.source_text: 唯有在这一点上，他特别像个无良少年。

en.t: In this point alone, he was especially like a delinquent boy.

units.source_text: 他在《不自欺记》里写过这么一段——

en.t: In Notes on Not Deceiving Oneself, he once wrote the following passage:
